$comment: Pinned upstream reference. Verified against the live repository on 2026-08-20; the tag SHAs below were read from the GitHub API, not transcribed from a document.

paper.title: Transparent reporting for agentic catalysis enabled by artificial intelligence: Community guidelines and a publication checklist
paper.$comment: Cite the published version. The infrastructure spec cited the ChemRxiv preprint; the paper is now published, and two of this project's investigators (Medford, Kitchin) are co-authors on it.

why_not_v2_0_0: The infrastructure spec pinned v2.0.0 (2026-02-07). That release predates the accepted manuscript.
v2.1.0 (2026-04-04) revised checklist item wording across all sections A1-D3, so item text under v2.0.0 is superseded.
v2.2.0 (2026-06-12) is described upstream as 'aligned with the accepted TRACE-AI manuscript'. Pinning anything earlier means citing item text that no longer matches the paper we cite alongside it.
For the record: the spec also gave v2.0.0's commit as 5d11e14, which is not that tag. v2.0.0 is 5101e248c00a695f07d4654ffd45ea38471ec231.

autonomy_scale.$comment: A0-A5, six levels. The infrastructure spec said A0-A4. This project operates at A1-A2 (human-gated).

sections.D: Tutorials, Notebooks, and Other Executable Artifacts (D1-D3)

bump_policy: Re-pinning is a deliberate act, not a dependency update. A new upstream release requires re-reading the crosswalk in this directory and re-checking enforcement.md, because revised item wording can change what we are claiming to satisfy. Record the reason in the standard's changelog.
